title: BIO 201 ( UNIZIK ) : CHEMICAL NATURE OF GENES AND GENE INTERACTIONS
subject: BIO 201

questions.question: The physical structure of a genome composed primarily of nucleic acid with structural proteins is called a?
questions.explanation: A chromosome is defined as the physical structure of a genome composed primarily of nucleic acid with structural proteins.

questions.question: The structure of an organism that contains instructions for growth and reproduction is known as a?
questions.explanation: A genome is defined as the structure of an organism that contains instructions for the organism's growth and reproduction.

questions.question: Elongated thread-like bodies clearly visible only when the cell is undergoing division are?
questions.explanation: Chromosomes are elongated, thread-like bodies clearly visible only when the cell is undergoing division.

questions.question: The basic units of heredity arranged linearly on chromosomes are called?
questions.explanation: The chromosomes bear, in linear arrangement, the basic units of heredity called genes.

questions.question: The chemical composition of chromosomes primarily includes DNA and which other substance?
questions.explanation: Chemically, the chromosomes are made up of DNA and proteins.

questions.question: The major proteins associated with chromosomes are known as?
questions.explanation: The major proteins associated with chromosomes are the histones.

questions.question: Histones are classified as basic proteins because they are rich in which amino acids?
questions.explanation: Histones are basic proteins because they are rich in such amino acids as lysine and arginine.

questions.question: Due to their amino acid composition, histones carry which type of electrical charge?
questions.explanation: Histones have a free amino group that can acquire a proton, making them positively charged.

questions.question: DNA is negatively charged because of the presence of which chemical group?
questions.explanation: DNA is negatively charged because of its many phosphate groups.

questions.question: How many types of histone proteins exist in eukaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: The histone proteins of all eukaryotic cells are of just five types namely H1, H2A, H2B, H3 and H4.

questions.question: Which of the following is a core histone?
questions.explanation: Core histones include H2A, H2B, H3 and H4.

questions.question: Which of the following is classified as a linker histone?
questions.explanation: H1 is the linker histone which basically locks DNA in place onto the nucleosome.

questions.question: The large, spherical body attached to certain chromosomes during interphase is the?
questions.explanation: One or more spherical bodies called nucleoli are attached to certain chromosomes.

questions.question: Cells that are very active in protein synthesis are characterized by having?
questions.explanation: Cells that are very active in protein synthesis have large nucleoli.

questions.question: The term chromosome was first introduced by which scientist?
questions.explanation: The term chromosome was first introduced by Waldeyer in 1888.

questions.question: Chromosomes occur as separate structures in the nucleus and are made of?
questions.explanation: Chromosomes are made of nucleo-protein.

questions.question: The process of mitosis was first worked out by which German botanist in 1875?
questions.explanation: Mitosis was first worked out by Strasburger, a German botanist in 1875.

questions.question: Each longitudinal half of a chromosome is called a?
questions.explanation: Each longitudinal half of the chromosome is called a chromatid.

questions.question: The structure of the chromosome may best be studied in which stages?
questions.explanation: The structure of the chromosome may best be studied in its metaphase or anaphase stage.

questions.question: The spindle fibers during cell division can originate from the cytoplasm or the?
questions.explanation: The spindle could originate from the nuclear sap or more frequently out of cytoplasm.

questions.question: The 46 chromosomes found in human cells have a combined length of approximately?
questions.explanation: The 46 chromosomes found in human cells have a combined length of 200 nm.

questions.question: If human chromosomes were uncoiled, the genetic material they contain would measure roughly?
questions.explanation: If the chromosomes were to be uncoiled, the genetic material they contain would measure roughly 2 meters.

questions.question: The average diameter of the nucleus is about?
questions.explanation: The average diameter of the nucleus is about 5 to 10 μm.

questions.question: Non-living viruses have chromosomes consisting of either DNA or?
questions.explanation: The non-living viruses have chromosomes consisting of either DNA or RNA.

questions.question: Among organisms with prokaryotic cells, chromosomes consist entirely of?
questions.explanation: Among organisms with prokaryotic cells, chromosomes consist entirely of DNA.

questions.question: Bacterial chromosomes differ from eukaryotic ones in being composed almost exclusively of DNA and in being?
questions.explanation: Bacterial chromosomes differ from those of eucaryotic organisms in being composed almost exclusively of DNA and in being circular.

questions.question: Bacterial DNA is combined with which histone-like protein?
questions.explanation: Bacterial DNA is combined with a histone-like protein called HU.

questions.question: The chromosomes of a eukaryotic cell consist primarily of DNA attached to a?
questions.explanation: The chromosomes of a eukaryotic cell consist primarily of DNA attached to a protein core.

questions.question: The number of chromosomes in body cells of a sexually reproducing organism is described as?
questions.explanation: Among sexually reproducing organisms, the number of chromosomes in the body (somatic) cells is diploid.

questions.question: Each gamete contains which number of chromosomes?
questions.explanation: Each gamete contains a haploid number of chromosomes.

questions.question: Human somatic cells contain how many chromosomes?
questions.explanation: In humans, the diploid number of chromosomes in somatic cells is 46.

questions.question: The common fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster has how many chromosomes?
questions.explanation: The common fruit fly has 8 chromosomes.

questions.question: The onion plant has how many chromosomes?
questions.explanation: The onion plant has 16 chromosomes.

questions.question: The failure of chromosomes to separate properly during cell division is called?
questions.explanation: The separation of chromosomes in cell division does not always proceed normally; this is known as nondisjunction.

questions.question: The presence of three chromosomes of one type in an otherwise diploid individual is called?
questions.explanation: The presence of three chromosomes of one type in an otherwise diploid individual is called trisomy.

questions.question: Cells or organisms that have more than two complete sets of chromosomes are said to be?
questions.explanation: Cells or organisms that have more than two complete sets of chromosomes are said to be polyploid.

questions.question: A description of the chromosome set of an organism is known as a?
questions.explanation: To study chromosomes, it is necessary to create a karyotype, which is a description of the chromosome set.

questions.question: Which drug disrupts the mitotic spindle and stops mitosis in metaphase?
questions.explanation: Dividing cells are treated with the drug colchicine, which disrupts the mitotic spindle and stops mitosis in metaphase.

questions.question: Karyotyping reveals distinctive bands on chromosomes that aid in identifying?
questions.explanation: Karyotyping reveals distinctive bands on chromosomes and aids in identifying homologs.

questions.question: Large scale changes in the linkages of genes are caused by chromosomal?
questions.explanation: Genes can be rearranged by chromosomal deletions, inversions and translocations, creating large scale changes in the linkages.

questions.question: A chromosome part breaking off and attaching to a nonhomologous chromosome is called a?
questions.explanation: A translocation occurs when part of a chromosome breaks off and attaches to a nonhomologous chromosome.

questions.question: A specific translocation between chromosomes 14 and 21 causes which syndrome?
questions.explanation: This is the cause of the Down syndrome following translocation between chromosomes 14 and 21.

questions.question: A chromosome segment that is cut out and reversed is known as a(n)?
questions.explanation: In an inversion, a segment of a chromosome is cut out and reversed.

questions.question: Inversions inhibit which genetic process?
questions.explanation: Inversions inhibit recombination by crossing over.

questions.question: Deletions of portions of the genome are generally considered?
questions.explanation: While duplications can be a source of novelty, deletions of portions of the genome are generally deleterious.

questions.question: Duplications of portions of the genome are a source of?
questions.explanation: Duplications are also a source of evolutionary novelty.

questions.question: Drosophila chromosomes are how many times larger than normal chromosomes?
questions.explanation: Drosophila chromosomes are 200 times larger than normal chromosomes.

questions.question: The first sex-linked trait discovered by Morgan was?
questions.explanation: The first sex-linked trait discovered by Morgan was the white eye colour in Drosophila.

questions.question: Genes located on the Y chromosome but not on the X are termed?
questions.explanation: Genes on the Y chromosome but not on the X are termed holandric.

questions.question: The study of the frequency and interaction of alleles and genes in populations is called?
questions.explanation: Population genetics is the study of the frequency and interaction of alleles and genes in populations.
